# OVERLOAD — Product Requirements Document

**Status:** Draft v0.7 · 2026-09-02 — adds §15 *LLM in the grain* (research-backed problems → solutions, Home v3 brief)
**Owner:** Vaibhav
**Type:** Personal strength-training tracker (single user, Hevy-inspired, deliberately simpler)
**Flow mockup (low-fi, clickable, real data):** https://claude.ai/code/artifact/bfb82488-a110-47ba-941b-a526210838cc · generated by `scripts/build_mockup.py` from the Hevy export
**Final frames:** Claude Design (claude.ai/design) — this PRD + the flow mockup are the handoff inputs. Design language: **iOS 26 Liquid Glass** on a black ground (§9).

---

## 1. Why

Hevy does too much: social feed, coaching, 400-exercise library, Pro paywalls. For one person lifting 3–5×/week the daily loop is:

1. Open app → see what you did, **know which workout is next** without thinking.
2. Log sets fast, one thumb, mid-set — last time's numbers already there — and get told the instant a set is a record.
3. Know **exactly what to beat** on every exercise, and whether you're actually progressing.

Everything else is secondary. OVERLOAD is that loop, nothing more, with room to grow.

## 2. Product principles

| Principle | Meaning in practice |
|---|---|
| **Zero decisions at the gym** | App picks the next workout. Last time's numbers are prefilled. You repeat or beat them. |
| **One thumb, one glance** | Every mid-set action lives in the bottom half of the screen. Big tap targets. No rest timer, no chrome. |
| **Overload is the product** | Every session gets one honest verdict against the last time you did that workout. A PR set is celebrated on the spot. |
| **Three colors, period** | Black, white, one neon. Neon means *action*, *progress* or *record* — never decoration. |
| **Simple graph** | One line per exercise. No toggles, no legends, no zoom. |
| **Your history is already here** | Hevy export imports on day one; nothing starts from zero. |
| **Phased** | Ship the loop first. Everything else waits. |

## 3. Non-goals (explicit)

- No social / feed / sharing. No multi-user, no coach mode.
- No rest timer (Phase 2 at the earliest — it's chrome).
- No authored form content. The dataset's 180×180 thumbnail identifies an exercise in the picker (Phase 1); its GIF + steps on the detail screen is Phase 2, loaded on demand.
- No cardio / step / calorie tracking.
- No cloud sync in Phase 1 (local-first; CSV in, CSV out).
- No paywall.

## 4. Core concepts (data model)

Terminology is deliberate and differs from Hevy:

- **Exercise** — name, body part, target muscle, equipment, load type (`weight+reps` | `bodyweight+reps` | `time`), optional thumbnail, `source: dataset | custom`. Seeded from the exercises-dataset (§4a); custom exercises are identical in shape.
- **Workout** — a *template*: name + ordered list of slots (exercise, target sets, rep range `lo–hi`). Standalone entity; there can be many; a workout can exist in no routine, one, or several.
- **Routine** — a named, ordered **loop of workouts** (e.g. `Legs → Shoulders and biceps → Back → Push 1`). Exactly one routine is *active*. The routine holds the loop **pointer**.
- **Session** — a performed workout: timestamp, duration, logged sets with actual weight/reps. Either *from* a workout (carries its name) or *fresh* (no template; can be saved as a workout afterwards).
- **Verdict** (derived, per session) — UP / DOWN / HELD / STALLED / BEST vs. the previous session of the same workout, plus per-set PRs. See §6.

## 4a. Exercise library

Source: **hasaneyldrm/exercises-dataset** (MIT data · © Gym visual media, see §13). Built by `scripts/build_exercises.py` → `data/exercises.json`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Records | 1,324 upstream → **1,312** after collapsing camera/gender variants (`(back pov)`, `(male)` …) |
| Kept per record | `id`, `name`, `bodyPart` (10), `target` (19), `equipment` (28, ~11 matter), `secondary[]`, `loadType`, `thumb`, `gif`, `steps[]` (English only) |
| Derived `loadType` | `cardio` → `time` · `body weight` / `assisted` → `bodyweight+reps` · else `weight+reps`. User-editable. |
| Size | 930 KB JSON (270 KB without steps) · thumbnails 8 MB total · GIFs 122 MB (never bundled) |
| Picker filters | **target** (primary chips) and **equipment** (secondary chips); body part is implied by target |
| Known gaps | no face pull, no cable fly crossover, no machine rear-delt fly … Custom exercises cover these; 7 of the user's 56 Hevy exercises are customs. |

Packaging: ship `exercises.json` + thumbnails in the app bundle (~9 MB). GIFs fetched lazily from the upstream repo path (Phase 2).

## 5. Feature: Auto next-workout selector

**Rule:** next workout = the workout after the one the last *completed from-template* session used, in the active routine's loop. Wraps.

- **Fresh sessions don't move the pointer.**
- **Skip / choose different** — starting any workout from S5 moves the pointer to it.
- **Stale routine** — no session in 10+ days → Home's dock asks "Restart from <first workout>?" instead of silently continuing.
- **Closing a session without finishing** keeps it as a draft and does not advance the pointer.

## 6. Feature: Progress verdicts (session vs. the last time you did this workout)

Two levels, one metric. Per **set**: PR. Per **session**: UP / DOWN / HELD / STALLED / BEST, compared against the previous session of the *same workout*. Reference implementation: `scripts/verdict.py` (it *is* the spec).

### 6.1 Metric — top-set e1RM
Per set `e1RM = w × (1 + r/30)` (Epley). Per exercise per session: the max over its working sets (warm-ups excluded). Bodyweight → best reps; time → best seconds. Used for *direction* within the same exercise, never as a true max, so its known inaccuracy at high reps doesn't matter here.

### 6.2 Session verdict
```
common  = exercises present in BOTH this session and the previous session of this workout
          need ≥ 2 and ≥ 50 % of today's exercises, else NO VERDICT ("new mix")
Δ       = mean over common of (e1RM_today − e1RM_prev) / e1RM_prev        # percent
verdict = UP if Δ > +1 %  ·  DOWN if Δ < −1 %  ·  HELD otherwise
STALLED = the last 3 verdicts for this workout contain no UP   (no-verdict sessions don't count)
BEST    = workout index is the highest ever for this workout AND verdict ≠ DOWN   (overrides UP/HELD)
```
- **Why a mean of percentages, not volume**: every exercise counts equally — a curl and a leg press each move the needle the same amount, and swapping one exercise doesn't swing the number. Tonnage is dominated by whichever machine lets you load the most (Calf Press is 38 % of a Legs session here).
- **Why ±1 %**: test-retest work puts the noise of reps-to-failure at ~1 rep (SEM), i.e. ~2.5–3 % e1RM on one exercise; averaged over 4–5 exercises that's ~1.2 %. Within the band is "same as last time". Wider (±1.5 %) tripled STALLED calls on this history; narrower is noise.
- **Workout index** = mean over exercises of `e1RM_today / baseline_exercise`, baseline = median e1RM of that exercise's first 3 sessions. It's a dimensionless "how strong is this workout today"; BEST = a new high. It also makes a natural per-workout long-term graph (Phase 2).
- Fresh sessions (no workout) get no verdict. Closing without finishing → no verdict, doesn't advance the loop.

### 6.3 PR — the reward moment (per set)
A set is a **PR** when its e1RM beats the exercise's all-time best, evaluated the instant ✓ is tapped. Only counts once the exercise has **≥ 3 prior sessions** (a first week on a new lift isn't a record). Row lights neon with the new e1RM, haptic; `PR` tag stays on the row and the card. This is the **only animation in the app**. PRs and the session verdict are independent: a session can be DOWN and still contain a PR.

### 6.4 Streak
Consecutive UP-or-BEST sessions of a workout. Resets on DOWN, not on HELD.

### 6.5 Validation on this history (2026-08-27, `scripts/verdict.py`)
Last 12 months, 186 sessions: **UP 89 · DOWN 29 · HELD 31 · STALLED 10 · BEST 14 · no verdict 13**. Sanity checks that came out right: Back is at its all-time best (BEST ×3, index 1.99 → 2.01 → 2.08); Push 1 has been STALLED since 20 Jul (index flat ~1.22 then 1.11); the 13 no-verdict sessions are all genuine exercise-set changes.

### 6.6 Evidence behind the choices
| Choice | Basis |
|---|---|
| Volume load rejected as the session metric | Scott et al. 2016 (*Sports Med*): volume load "does not account for" the difficulty of the reps at a load; SBS: volume load only comparable at equal %1RM; Refalo et al. 2022 meta-analysis: *set volume* likely more potent than volume load; Baz-Valle et al. 2021 (*JSCR*): sets near failure are an adequate volume measure for 6–20+ reps. |
| e1RM as the per-exercise metric | Plotkin et al. 2022 (*PeerJ*): load progression and rep progression are equally viable — e1RM credits both. RTS/Helms: e1RM is for *trends*, not absolute maxes. |
| e1RM used for direction only | Marzagão 2026 (Fitbod, arXiv, 303k sets): Epley came from a poundage chart, fixed factor, inconsistency grows with reps; a weight-dependent formula is 17–22 % more consistent. Within-exercise comparison sidesteps most of this. Upgrade path: swap the formula, nothing else changes. |
| ±1 % noise band, 3-session STALL | PLOS One 2022 test-retest: reps-to-failure SEM ≈ 1 rep at 80–90 % 1RM, ≈ 1.5 at 70 %; day-to-day strength CV 3.5–4 %. |
| No self-rated effort in Phase 1 | Session-RPE (Day et al. 2004; Haddad et al. 2017 review) is valid and reliable but needs a rating after every session; RIR-RPE (Zourdos et al. 2016) needs one per set. Phase 2 option, not a Phase 1 input. |
| No app does this | Hevy: per-set PRs only (weight, e1RM, set volume, reps, duration). Boostcamp: DOTS strength score. JuggernautAI: asks you to rate the session 5–10. Alpha Progression: per-set recommendations. |

Sources: [Scott 2016](https://vuir.vu.edu.au/32754/1/Monitor%20Strength%20Review.pdf) · [Baz-Valle 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30063555/) · [Refalo 2022](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40279-022-01784-y) · [Plotkin 2022](https://peerj.com/articles/14142/) · [Marzagão 2026](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.17495) · [PLOS One 2022 test-retest](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0268074) · [Haddad 2017 sRPE review](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnins.2017.00612/full) · [Zourdos 2016](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26049792/) · [SBS on volume](https://www.strongerbyscience.com/the-new-approach-to-training-volume/) · [Hevy PRs](https://help.hevyapp.com/hc/en-us/articles/35649367857175) · [Boostcamp](https://www.boostcamp.app/vs/strong) · [JuggernautAI](https://www.garagegymreviews.com/juggernautai-review)

## 7. Feature: Simple graph

- One SVG line, e1RM over the last 12 sessions. Latest point filled neon. STALL windows hatched.
- Tap a point → one tooltip: date · top set · e1RM.
- Under it: **Best · Last · Δ 30 d**. That's all the analytics.

## 7a. Feature: Hevy import & sync

3.4 years of history already live in Hevy. Importing it means overload state, streaks, PRs, graphs and the calendar are real on day one, and workouts/routine can be reconstructed instead of typed.

### 7a.1 Source — Hevy CSV export (one row per set)
```
title, start_time, end_time, description, exercise_title, superset_id, exercise_notes,
set_index, set_type, weight_kg, reps, distance_km, duration_seconds, rpe
```
- Session key = `(title, start_time)`; `start_time` local, `"27 Aug 2026, 00:36"`.
- `weight_kg` empty + `reps` → bodyweight set. `duration_seconds` → time set.
- `set_type` ∈ `normal | warmup | failure | dropset` (this export: 100 % `normal`). `superset_id`, `rpe`, `distance_km` present but empty here.

### 7a.2 Import algorithm (`scripts/import_hevy.py` is the spike)
1. Parse → group by session key → one **Session** per group, sets ordered by `set_index`.
2. Map `exercise_title` → library exercise via `data/hevy_aliases.json` (curated Hevy name → dataset id; token-match fallback with a confidence score). Below threshold → **review sheet**: pick a library exercise or create custom.
3. `warmup` sets stored, excluded from overload calc.
4. **Idempotent**: re-importing the same CSV is a no-op; new sessions append. This is the Phase 1 "sync".
5. Recompute e1RM series, badges, streaks, PRs → Home cards, week dots, Calendar, S4 graphs populate.

Result on this export: 56 exercise names → **49 mapped, 7 custom, 6 flagged for a look**.

### 7a.3 Workout & routine reconstruction (first import)
- Titles used ≥ 3× in the last 120 days become **Workouts**: slots = exercises present in ≥ 50 % of that title's last 6 sessions (ordered by average position), sets = median count, rep range = p25–p75 of logged reps, duration estimate = median session length.
- They form the initial **Routine** loop, ordered by last-performed ascending, so the pointer lands on the least-recently-done workout. On this export: `Legs → Shoulders and biceps → Back → Push 1`.
- All other titles become workouts outside the loop. User confirms/edits in S5/S6.

### 7a.4 Sync beyond CSV
- **Phase 1**: manual CSV re-import (Hevy → Settings → Export data → S8 "Import from Hevy").
- **Phase 2**: Hevy API polling on app open (`api.hevyapp.com/v1/workouts`, needs a Hevy Pro API key — *verify before committing*). Same pipeline, JSON instead of CSV.

### 7a.5 This export, profiled (2026-08-27)
470 sessions · 2023-03-29 → 2026-08-27 · 56 distinct exercises · 6,078 sets · avg 5.1 exercises / 48 min. Titles: Legs 108 · Push 1 89 · Back 77 · Shoulders 39 · Pull 37 · Shoulders and biceps 36 · Back 2.0 27 · … Monthly volume fell from ~20 (late 2025) to 8 (Aug 2026).

| # | Screen | Purpose | Key elements |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | **Home** | See history, start | Top: date + week dots (tap → S8). **Session cards**, newest first: workout name · when · duration, then each exercise line = name · `PR` tag · top set · badge (row → S4, card → S3 read-only). **Glass dock** pinned at bottom: `START NEXT · <WORKOUT>` (neon) + `Fresh workout` (outline). Tab bar. |
| S2 | **Active session** | Log | Header: workout name · elapsed · close. Per exercise: name + badge, hint `Last <top set> · best e1RM <b>`, set rows `# · prev · kg · reps · ✓` prefilled with last session's sets. **PR row state** (§6.3). | S3 | **Session summary** | Payoff | Name, time. Three numbers: duration · **PRs** (neon) · went-UP count. Per-exercise rows with `PR`, top set, streak, badge. Fresh session → `Save as workout`. `Next up · <WORKOUT>`. `DONE` (neon) commits + advances the pointer. |

Sections: **In your workouts** (with last top set) · Recent · All. Row = 40 px thumb · name · `target · equipment` · `+`. Tap adds and returns. `Create custom exercise`. Attribution line. |

Navigation: floating glass **tab bar** — Home · Exercises · Routines. Exercises tab = S7's list landing on S4. Active session is a full-screen modal. S8 hangs off the week dots, not a tab.

## 9. Design system — three colors on Liquid Glass

```
BLACK  #000000   ground
WHITE  #FFFFFF   text, outlines, inactive  — opacity tiers 100 / 60 / 30 / 12 % are the only greys
NEON   #CCFF00   action · progress · record  (alternates: #39FF14 · #00FFD1 — one token)
```

- **Liquid Glass (iOS 26)**: the dock, tab bar, picker sheet and slot-edit sheet are glass surfaces floating over the black ground; content scrolls beneath them. Cards are flat panels (#0C0C0C), not glass — glass is reserved for controls so it stays legible.
- Neon is never a background for text longer than one word/number. Neon text on black for numbers; black text on neon for buttons and PR rows.
- Type: system display (SF) for the UI, **tabular numerals everywhere**; a mono face for set rows and stats is acceptable if it reads better on glass.
- Radius: 14 px buttons/cards, 22 px glass containers, 999 px pills. 1 px white-12 % dividers. No shadows — glass provides depth.
- Motion: **only** the PR moment and the STALL dot. Nothing else moves.

## 10. Phases

### Phase 1 — The loop (design now)
S1–S8, local storage, exercise library (thumbnails bundled), custom exercises, **Hevy CSV import with workout/routine reconstruction**, month calendar, CSV export. Auto-selector + overload tracker + PR moment + simple graph.

### Phase 2 — Refinement
- **Progression targets**: +1 rep / +2.5 kg rule with per-exercise increment (skipped in Phase 1 by decision)
- Rest timer (opt-in, per workout)
- Supersets / circuits (slot groups sharing a rest)
- RPE per set, warm-up flag (excluded from overload)
- Deload / swap flow from STALL (auto-generate a −10 % variant)
- Exercise detail: GIF (lazy-loaded) + instruction steps
- Hevy API sync (needs Pro key)
- Body-weight log (same graph component), notes per session / exercise
- Watch complication

### Phase 3 — Growth
- Cloud backup
- Routine templates (PPL, Upper/Lower, 5/3/1-style progression rules)
- Per-exercise progression rule (double progression, linear, wave)

## 11. Open questions

*Decided 2026-08-27: platform = iOS 26 native (SwiftUI + Liquid Glass); supersets → Phase 2; progression targets → Phase 2.*

1. **Units** — kg default; lb toggle Phase 1 or 2?
2. **Neon pick** — #CCFF00 (acid) / #39FF14 (green) / #00FFD1 (cyan). One token.
3. **Bundle thumbnails?** 8 MB in the app for picker clarity vs. a text-only picker. *(Assumption: bundle.)*
4. **Hevy API** — does the account have Pro / an API key? Decides whether Phase 2 sync is automatic.
5. **Alias review** — 6 Hevy names auto-mapped at low confidence (`data/hevy_aliases.json`, `"review": true`); eyeball before first real import.

## 12. Success criteria (personal)

- Start the next workout in **1 tap** from cold open; a fresh one in 1 tap + picker.
- Log a set in ≤ 1 tap when repeating last time.
- A PR is visible the moment the set is checked — no digging.
- Answer "am I progressing on this lift?" in ≤ 3 s from a Home card.

## 15. LLM in the grain (v0.7)

**Direction (decided 2026-09-02):** Routine and Workout stay the core entities. The LLM is a layer **on top of** routine/workout status and engine data. It is *not* a feature, tab, card, chatbot, or "Coach" brand — reasoning appears **in the grain of the app**: one more line of type inside components that already exist, in the same mono/sage language, visible only when it has something non-obvious to say.

### 15.1 Problems found → solutions proposed

Research 2026-09-02: two web sweeps — (a) what lifters ask for / complain about (Reddit signal via roundups, r/Fitness FAQ, app reviews of Hevy/Strong/Fitbod/Jefit), (b) the AI-fitness landscape and its reception (Whoop Coach, Strava Athlete Intelligence, Fitbod, JuggernautAI, Hevy Trainer, SmartGym, Apple Workout Buddy).

| # | Problem (evidence) | Our solution |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Logging-vs-coaching gap** — every tracker "logs what you do, doesn't tell you what to do next" (Hevy/Strong reviews); the single most recurrent complaint | Reasoning attaches to what the engine already decides: verdicts, next-workout pointer, PRs. The app keeps deciding; the LLM explains and contextualizes |
| P2 | **"I'm stalled, what do I do?"** is the #1 lifter question (r/Fitness FAQ, plateau content industry) | The engine's STALLED verdict grows grounded options inline on that workout's card (deload / rep-range change / substitution) — user-confirmed actions, never auto-applied |
| P3 | **ChatGPT-as-trainer fails on memory** — "doesn't remember the shoulder you tweaked in March… every plan floats free of the one before" ; people hack Hevy MCP servers to fix this | Our LLM reads a **CoachContext** built from the engine: routine cycle state, per-workout verdict trails, e1RM trends, PRs. It always knows the history because the history is the input |
| P4 | **Generic AI praise gets mocked** — Strava's "great effort!" became a meme; data-literate users resent restated obviousness | Only cycle-over-cycle, non-obvious statements ("quiet gains": e1RM up while weight×reps look flat). If there is nothing non-obvious, **say nothing** — absence is a valid state |
| P5 | **Hallucinated data kills trust** — Whoop's AI invented caffeine/elevation entries; users quit over one fabricated fact | The LLM **never computes or invents a number**. Engine computes (Swift, deterministic, tested); LLM narrates the precomputed payload only. Rendering is display-only text |
| P6 | **No "why" behind recommendations** — Hevy Trainer criticized for unexplainable output; SmartGym praised for reason-attached suggestions | Every verdict chip (UP/DOWN/HELD/STALLED/BEST) becomes tappable → a grounded explanation citing the actual sets behind it |
| P7 | **Speed is sacred** — lifters reject anything adding taps mid-set | Zero LLM surface inside the live session. Reasoning lives on Home, workout cards, and the summary — never between sets |
| P8 | **Prescriptive AI causes real harm** — Runna injury wave; >half of AI fitness-chatbot advice rated problematic in studies | Descriptive + optional, never prescriptive-silent. The LLM suggests with reasons; only the user changes a load, ever |

### 15.2 Where reasoning lives (no new chrome)

1. **Hero insight line (Home)** — after a cycle completes (routine pointer wraps), the hero's context line carries one sentence of cycle-over-cycle insight in place of the static "next · beat" line. Mono 11, ink-muted with sage keywords. Disappears mid-cycle if there's nothing to say.
2. **Verdict chips → "why" sheet** — chips on workout cards, session summaries, and calendar rows open a short grounded explanation (the sets, the deltas, the streak that produced the verdict).
3. **Stalled workout card** — an inline reasoning line + 2–3 option chips under the stats row of that card only, in its stalled state. Options deep-link (start deload variant, open workout edit, pick substitution) and require confirmation.
4. **Summary (S3)** — one explanatory line under the verdict badge: why this session earned it.
5. *(Phase 2)* **Ask-history** — natural-language questions over the store ("when did I last squat 100?"), entered from Calendar search. Not part of Home v3.

### 15.3 Grounding contract

```json
CoachContext {
  routine:   { name, cycle, position: "3/4", next },
  workouts: [{ name, verdictTrail: ["UP","HELD","STALLED"], index: {last, best},
               sessions, exercises: [{ name, e1rmTrend, flatStreak, topSet }] }],
  lastCycle: { sessions: [...top sets...], prs: [...], skipped: [...] },
  deltas:    { thisCycleVsPrev: ... }
}
```
~2 KB, fully precomputed by the existing engine (§6). Prompt rule: *every number in the output must appear in the payload.*

### 15.4 States

| State | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Cycle just wrapped | Fresh hero insight + card lines where warranted |
| Mid-cycle, nothing new | Reasoning lines absent — the v0.6 layout, unchanged |
| < 1 full cycle of data | No LLM surfaces at all |
| Offline / API error | Show last cached lines or nothing; never a spinner or error chrome |

### 15.5 Out of scope

Form checks (camera), auto-adjusted loads, daily digests/motivation, nutrition, a chat-bubble UI, streaks/badges. "Coach" naming anywhere.

### 15.6 Tech

Claude API (Haiku-class) — the target phone (iPhone 15, non-Pro) has no Apple Intelligence, so on-device Foundation Models are unavailable; cost at cycle-cadence rounds to pennies/month. Responses cached per (routine, cycle) and (session id); regenerate on new data only. e2e determinism via a `--coach-fixture` launch argument returning canned lines (suite never hits the network).

### 15.7 Design brief — Home v3 (for Claude Design)

Design the Home screen (S1) with reasoning **woven in typographically**, zero new containers:
- Keep: fixed header (icon · date · week dots), routine hero (name · cycle · segments · index chart · stats row), workout cards in loop order, single SLIDE TO START, resume bar when live.
- Explore: (a) the hero insight line — where one grounded sentence lives inside the existing hero without adding a box; (b) the stalled card state — reasoning line + option chips inside the card's current anatomy; (c) tappable verdict chips — an affordance that reads as "there's a why here" at mono-11 scale; (d) the why-sheet itself — glass sheet, sets cited in mono, one screen, no scroll.
- Tone: statements, not cheerleading. Sage for the signal word, ink-muted for the rest. If a state has nothing to say, the design must look complete without it (absence-first).
